title: Listen (Rule, Prologue)
hook: the Rule begins with listen, with the ear of your heart

segments.voice: Yesterday, many schools: Thomas beside Augustine, Bonaventure and Scotus, kept side by side. Your line was many teachers.

Nod. Say mm-hm. Plan your reply while the other person is still talking. Half-listening takes almost no effort, and it can pass for the real thing for a long time. A new block begins today: the great religious orders, the communities of monks, friars and sisters who share a way of life. First, the Benedictines, and a small book written for monks in Italy long ago. Its very first word is not pray. Not work. Not obey. Listen.
screen: `HALF-LISTENING.` → `A NEW BLOCK: THE GREAT ORDERS.` → `THE FIRST WORD: LISTEN.`

segments.voice: Back on day eighty-seven you met Benedict and his sister Scholastica, his twin, tradition says. Tradition gives him the Rule, a short book to guide monks living together in Italy. Monks call it simply the Rule. It covers prayer and work, meals and sleep, guests and the sick, and how to settle a quarrel. But it opens like a letter from a father to a son. In Latin: inclina aurem cordis tui. Listen, my son, to the teaching of the master, and bend down the ear of your heart. It's the posture of someone leaning in to catch a quiet voice, a parent bent over a cot. And it's the ear of the heart, not just the ears on your head: letting what you hear reach the place where you decide things. The Prologue says this listening should turn into doing, and that the one speaking is finally God. It borrows a psalm, in the Douay-Rheims: "To day if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts." Notice the order. Before the long list of chapters, before the schedule, before a single bell rings, there's a posture: lean in. A rule, for Benedict, isn't a cage of instructions. It's a shared way of listening, kept day after day, so a whole community can hear together. Benedictine monks and nuns still read the Rule aloud together, and each time they come back around to its start, the first thing they hear is: listen.
screen: `A SHORT BOOK FOR MONKS.` · `BEND DOWN THE EAR OF YOUR HEART.` · `LISTENING TURNS INTO DOING.` · `A RULE IS A WAY OF LISTENING.` · then, large: `HARDEN NOT YOUR HEARTS.`

segments.voice: Start with the sounds around you, the hum of a room, a car outside, your own breathing, and just lean toward them, without naming or judging. Then bring to mind the person you'll talk with next, and imagine giving them that same attention: no planning your reply, no phone, just leaning in. If you pray, ask to hear God's voice in whatever comes.
Rule. Saint Benedict's short book for monks living together, which opens with one word: listen, with the ear of your heart. Today's word.
Your line: the ear of the heart. Before the schedule and the bells, Benedict asks for a posture. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Benedictine monks and nuns hear passages of the Rule read aloud in community, and oblates and other laypeople read it at home.

chat.says: What's the very first word of Saint Benedict's Rule for monks?
options: Listen: bend down the ear of your heart, so what you hear can turn into doing.
Obey: the Rule sets out the abbot's authority before anything else is said.
Pray: the Rule opens with the hours of prayer the monks keep each day.
chat.meaning: The Rule opens: listen, and bend down the ear of your heart. Before any schedule, Benedict sets a posture: lean in.

notes: The Rule's opening is paraphrased (Gasquet 1909 is the outline's translation, but its exact wording wasn't verified, so nothing is quoted). Latin 'Obsculta (Ausculta), o fili, praecepta magistri, et inclina aurem cordis tui' — confirm spelling and the gloss 'bend down the ear of your heart'.
'Tradition gives the Rule to Saint Benedict, who gathered monks in Italy' — no dates or place names (Subiaco, Monte Cassino) given. Confirm.
The Prologue's use of Psalm 94(95):8 — confirm it is cited there. Douay-Rheims wording to confirm.
'Benedictine monks and nuns still read from the Rule each day' — custom of daily reading (e.g. at chapter); confirm phrasing.
Index word is 'Rule' while the title is 'Listen'; the script uses 'Rule' as today's word as required.

Editor pass: 'read from the Rule each day ... they begin, every time, by being told to listen' was wrong (the Rule is read through in portions, so the Prologue is not heard every day); now 'each time they come back around to its start'; 'each day' dropped from voice and howItsDone; practice 'Imagine' changed to 'Plan to'.
